newsitem.title: EGYPT: Separating Hebron breaks peace agreement - Egypt.
newsitem.headline: Separating Hebron breaks peace agreement - Egypt.

text.p: Egyptian Foreign Minister Amr Moussa said on Monday that Israel was breaking its peace accord with the PLO by separating the West Bank town of Hebron.
"The ongoing separation, and what could form a fence around or in Hebron, is considered a break of the existing agreement," Moussa told reporters.

Palestinians accuse Israel of imposing collective punishment by putting up concrete barriers and isolating the 20,000 Palestinians living on the Israeli-held side from the 80,000 who live under self-rule.
Israel handed over 80 percent of Hebron to the PLO in January under a peace deal.
Hebron has been the scene of almost daily unrest for more than two weeks. Israeli soldiers have wounded scores of Palestinians in protests. Several soldiers have also been hurt.

Israel's central area commander responsible for the West Bank, Major-General Uzi Dayan, threatened to take further retaliatory action against Palestinians if they resumed throwing stones and petrol bombs.

"Working for peace is the important matter, rather than building fences and carrying out measures that lead to great frustration among the Palestinian people," Moussa added after meeting Mordechai Bar-On, a leader of the Israeli movement Peace Now.
Bar-On told reporters that he was not optimistic about a breakthrough in the peace process.
Formal peace talks have been frozen since Israel broke ground on a Jewish settlement in Arab East Jerusalem four months ago.
"We are mobilising Israeli public opinion to move towards early elections that bring a new government to work for peace," Bar-On said.
